faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate on the timesheet page. The calculator multiplies it by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks to give an annual gross figure. faqs.q: Does the salary calculator WA include casual loading?

faqs.q: How is tax calculated in the salary calculator WA?

bodyMarkdown:
## Salary Calculator WA: From Hourly Rate to Annual, Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Whether you are negotiating a salary offer or checking what your current hourly rate means over a full year, the **salary calculator WA** gives you a clear picture. It converts your base hourly rate into annual gross pay, then estimates tax, Medicare and superannuation. The calculator assumes a standard 38‑hour week – the same hours the Fair Work Ombudsman uses for the National Minimum Wage – and works for both full‑time and part‑time employees.

### How the hourly‑to‑annual conversion works

The formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a 38‑hour week that becomes **hourly rate × 38 × 52**. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Multiply by 38 gives $1,004.90 per week, and by 52 gives $52,254.80 per year. The [timesheet](/) on this site does the maths for you – just type your base hourly rate and the calculator shows the annual, fortnightly and weekly figures.

If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours in the calculator. The default of 38 hours matches the ordinary hours in many awards and the National Employment Standards. For part‑time employees, enter your actual weekly hours. The calculator always multiplies by 52 weeks, so it assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave.

### Using the salary calculator WA for your situation

The **salary calculator WA** is especially useful if you are looking at Western Australian pay rates. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, average weekly earnings for full‑time adult ordinary time in Western Australia were $2,227.40 per week in May 2026. That is an average across all industries and occupations – not a median for any specific job. If your hourly rate is different, the calculator will show how your own pay compares on an annual basis.

For casual employees, the calculator includes a checkbox for 25% casual loading. Casual loading is paid on top of the base hourly rate as compensation for not receiving paid leave. The National Minimum Wage for casuals from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour (the base rate of $26.44 plus 25% loading). Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading – tick the box and the calculator adds it automatically. The loading is the minimum required by the Fair Work Ombudsman; some awards provide higher loading.

### Tax and Medicare on your annual figure

Once you have your annual gross pay, the **salary calculator WA** estimates the tax you will pay as a resident for 2026–27. The tax‑free threshold is $18,200. Above that, the rates are:

- 15% for income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% for income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% for income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% for income above $190,000

The calculator also deducts the Medicare levy at 2% of your taxable income. It uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed when this calculator was prepared. If you are a single person with no dependants, the Medicare levy applies to all taxable income above a certain amount; the calculator applies the standard 2% rate. The result is an estimate of your take‑home pay – it does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown, see the [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Superannuation paid on top

Superannuation is not deducted from your pay; it is paid on top by your employer. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). The **salary calculator WA** shows an estimated super amount based on your annual gross pay. For example, on the National Minimum Wage annual of $52,254.80, super would be $6,270.58 per year (12% of ordinary earnings). If your annual pay exceeds the maximum contribution base, super is capped at $32,499.60 (12% of $270,830).

Super is paid on ordinary earnings, which includes your base hourly rate and any casual loading, but not overtime or expense reimbursements. The calculator assumes your entire annual gross pay is ordinary earnings. For more on how super interacts with your pay package, visit the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Important disclaimers

The **salary calculator WA** provides an estimate only. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Annual pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

Always check your specific award or agreement for your correct rate. The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Award rates are often higher and may include penalty rates, allowances, and different casual loading. For award‑specific information, see the [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has the latest Fair Work Commission decisions.

### Fortnightly pay and budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. The **salary calculator WA** shows your fortnightly gross pay as weekly pay multiplied by two. For the National Minimum Wage, that is $2,009.80 per fortnight before tax. After tax and Medicare, your take‑home will be lower – the calculator estimates that too. Knowing your fortnightly figure helps with budgeting and comparing salary offers. If you receive a salary offer expressed as an annual figure, you can work backwards: divide by 52 to get weekly, then by your usual hours to find the equivalent hourly rate.

### Final thoughts

The **salary calculator WA** is a practical tool for anyone in Western Australia or elsewhere who wants to understand the full picture of their pay. Use it alongside the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to see how your rate compares with state and national averages. Remember that averages are not medians – your job may pay differently. For job‑specific information, the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page has guidance on finding award classifications and market rates.

Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman or the Australian Taxation Office for personalised advice. The calculator is a starting point, not a determination of your pay or tax.
